newsitem.title: UK: Britain's SFA says to begin action against Fidelity.
newsitem.headline: Britain's SFA says to begin action against Fidelity.

text.p: British financial regulator the Securities and Futures Authority (SFA) said on Friday it would start disciplinary action against Fidelity Brokerage Services over problems with its customer service performance.

The watchdog also extended to the end of April restrictions on Fidelity Brokerage Services, the British retail stockbroking arm of the U.S. fund management giant, preventing it from taking on new direct customers or introduce new business services. But it was satisfied the firm had resources and backing to ensure investors' monies and securities "are not in any jeopardy".

Last November Fidelity promised to restore "satisfactory" service to clients by this months, after computer problems forced it to stop taking new customers. It said system problems had resulted in accounting and reconciliation difficulties and promised compensation to any customers who lost out as a result.

The SFA said in statement on Friday that "good progress has been made, but further work is still required before SFA can be confident that Fidelity Brokerage Services is offering a level of customer service which is consistently satisfactory".
It said it would continue to monitor closely the customer service performance of the firm and would oversee the resolution of outstanding customer complaints and enquiries.

In addition it said it would take into account the speed with which Fidelity brought "the outstanding matters to a satisfactory conclusion in determining the nature and extent of...disciplinary proceedings and the scale of the penalty which is sought".
